digest.lead: Anthropic is restricting third-party tools like OpenClaw from working with Claude Code subscriptions, sparking significant developer backlash.
digest.summary: Meanwhile, Claude Code v2.1.92 ships with new enterprise features and Bedrock integration, while researchers demonstrate Claude's security bug-finding capabilities in popular editors.

stories.headline: Anthropic Restricts Third-Party Tools Access to Claude Subscriptions
stories.summary: Anthropic is limiting the use of third-party harnesses and tools like OpenClaw with Claude subscriptions [3][4]. The policy change has generated significant discussion in the developer community, with over 555 points and 485 comments on Hacker News [4].
key_points: OpenClaw and similar third-party tools will no longer work with Claude Code subscriptions
The restriction appears to be part of broader limitations on third-party harnesses
stories.perspectives: The community response suggests strong opposition to this policy change, though Anthropic's reasoning for the restriction hasn't been publicly detailed.
stories.impact: This significantly affects developers who rely on OpenClaw and similar tools for their Claude workflows, forcing them to either switch tools or reconsider their subscription plans.

sources.title: Anthropic to limit Using third-party harnesses with Claude subscriptions
Tell HN: Anthropic no longer allowing Claude Code subscriptions to use OpenClaw

stories.headline: Claude Code v2.1.92 Adds Enterprise Security and Bedrock Integration
stories.summary: The latest Claude Code release introduces enterprise-focused features including a fail-closed policy for managed settings and an interactive Bedrock setup wizard [1]. Subscription users also gain detailed cost breakdowns with per-model and cache-hit analytics [1].
key_points: New `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` policy ensures enterprise security by blocking startup until managed settings are verified
Interactive Bedrock wizard simplifies AWS authentication and model configuration from the login screen
Enhanced cost tracking shows per-model usage and cache efficiency for subscription users
stories.impact: Enterprise teams gain better security controls and AWS integration, while subscription users get improved visibility into their Claude usage costs and patterns.

stories.headline: Claude Discovers Critical RCE Vulnerabilities in Vim and Emacs
stories.summary: Security researchers used Claude AI to identify remote code execution bugs in popular text editors Vim and Emacs that can be triggered simply by opening malicious files [5]. The discovery demonstrates AI's growing role in automated vulnerability research.
stories.impact: This showcases Claude's potential for security research and highlights serious vulnerabilities that could affect millions of developers using these editors daily.

sources.title: Claude AI finds Vim, Emacs RCE bugs that trigger on file open

stories.headline: Developer Creates AI-Powered Travel Hacking Toolkit
stories.summary: A developer has open-sourced a travel hacking toolkit that uses AI for points optimization and trip planning, generating community interest with 58 points and 27 comments on Hacker News [2]. The project demonstrates practical applications of AI in personal finance and travel planning.
stories.impact: Shows how developers are building specialized AI tools for niche use cases like travel optimization, potentially inspiring similar domain-specific applications.

sources.title: Show HN: Travel Hacking Toolkit – Points search and trip planning with AI

stories.headline: Use forceRemoteSettingsRefresh policy to ensure fresh configuration on startup
stories.summary: This setting forces Claude Code CLI to fetch the latest remote managed settings before starting and exits if the fetch fails. This ensures your CLI always runs with the most current configuration and prevents running with stale settings that might cause issues.
actionable_steps: Open your Claude Code CLI configuration
Restart the CLI to verify it blocks startup until fresh settings are fetched

stories.headline: Use @-mentions to give Claude Code precise file context
stories.summary: Boris Cherny, creator of Claude Code, recommends using @-mentions to point Claude at specific files instead of letting it search. This dramatically reduces token usage and improves accuracy since Claude works with the exact files you intend rather than guessing from project structure.
actionable_steps: Type @ in Claude Code to see a file picker with fuzzy search
Select the specific files relevant to your task before writing your prompt
Combine multiple @-mentions for cross-file tasks like refactoring

stories.headline: Enable PowerShell tool for Windows development workflows
stories.summary: Claude Code now includes an opt-in PowerShell tool that allows Windows users to execute PowerShell commands directly through Claude. This provides native Windows command-line access for system administration and development tasks.
actionable_steps: Update Claude Code to version 2.1.84 or later
Enable the PowerShell tool in your settings as a preview feature

stories.headline: Use /powerup command to learn Claude Code features interactively
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.90 introduced the /powerup command that provides interactive lessons with animated demos to help you learn Claude Code features. This is particularly useful for new users who want to quickly understand the tool's capabilities through hands-on tutorials.
actionable_steps: Update Claude Code to version 2.1.90 or later
Type `/powerup` in the Claude Code interface
Follow the interactive lessons and animated demos to learn features

stories.headline: Use defer permission in PreToolUse hooks to pause headless sessions
stories.summary: You can now pause headless Claude Code sessions at tool calls and resume them later with permission evaluation. This allows for better control over automated workflows that need human approval.
actionable_steps: Set up a PreToolUse hook in your Claude Code configuration
Return 'defer' as the permission decision in the hook
The hook will re-evaluate the tool call upon resumption
